events.title: Indus Valley Civilization
events.description: The Indus Valley Civilization (also known as Harappan Civilization) was one of the world's four ancient civilizations, located in present-day Pakistan and northwestern India. Harappa and Mohenjo-daro were its major cities, featuring advanced urban planning, drainage systems, and script.

events.title: Aryan Migration
events.description: Aryan tribes migrated from Central Asia into the Indian subcontinent, bringing Sanskrit and Vedic religion. This period saw the beginnings of the caste system, which profoundly influenced Indian social structure.

events.title: Vedic Period
events.description: The Vedic period was foundational for Indian religious and philosophical thought. Four Vedas (Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda) were compiled during this time, forming the basis of Hinduism.

events.title: Birth of Buddha
events.description: Siddhartha Gautama, founder of Buddhism, was born in present-day Nepal. He attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at age 35 and founded Buddhism, advocating compassion, wisdom, and the path to liberation. Buddhism later spread to East and Southeast Asia, becoming one of the world's major religions.

events.title: Mahavira Founds Jainism
events.description: Mahavira founded Jainism, advocating non-violence (ahimsa), asceticism, and spiritual liberation. Jainism significantly influenced Indian culture and philosophy, maintaining importance in India today.

events.title: Alexander Invades India
events.description: Alexander the Great led his army to invade northwestern India, reaching Punjab region. Though brief, the conquest promoted Greek-Indian cultural exchange, influencing later Gandhara art.

events.title: Mauryan Empire Founded
events.description: Chandragupta Maurya established the Mauryan Empire, unifying most of northern India. This was India's first unified great empire, with capital at Pataliputra (modern Patna).

events.title: Ashoka's Accession
events.description: Emperor Ashoka ascended to the throne and conquered Kalinga, but the war's cruelty led him to embrace Buddhism. He subsequently promoted Buddhism throughout his empire, erecting pillars and rock edicts, facilitating Buddhism's spread to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia. Ashoka's reign was one of ancient India's most glorious periods.

events.title: Mauryan Empire Falls
events.description: Mauryan Empire was overthrown by Shunga dynasty, India again fragmented. Following centuries saw succession of multiple dynasties including Shunga, Andhra.

events.title: Kushan Empire Rises
events.description: Kushan Empire emerged in modern Afghanistan, Pakistan, and northwestern India, becoming important Silk Road state. Kushans promoted Buddhist art development (especially Gandhara art) and Buddhism's spread to Central Asia and China.

events.title: Gupta Empire Founded
events.description: Chandragupta I established the Gupta Empire, inaugurating India's 'Golden Age.' During the Gupta period, science, mathematics, astronomy, literature, and arts reached unprecedented development, and Hindu culture experienced revival and prosperity.

events.title: Gupta Scientific Achievements
events.description: During Gupta period, mathematician Aryabhata invented the concept of zero and positional notation, astronomer Aryabhata calculated pi. These achievements later spread to Arab world and Europe, making enormous contributions to human civilization.

events.title: Faxian Visits India
events.description: Chinese Eastern Jin monk Faxian traveled to India to seek Buddhist texts, spending about 10 years in India learning Sanskrit scriptures. His travelogue 'Record of Buddhist Kingdoms' detailed India's society, religion, and culture of that time.

events.title: Gupta Empire Declines
events.description: Under Hunnic (Hephthalite) invasions and internal fragmentation, Gupta Empire gradually declined. India again entered period of fragmentation with multiple local kingdoms.

events.title: Reign of Harsha
events.description: Harsha unified most of northern India, establishing powerful empire. He protected Buddhism and Hinduism, promoting cultural development. Chinese Tang monk Xuanzang visited India during this period, receiving Harsha's hospitality.

events.title: Xuanzang Visits India
events.description: Tang monk Xuanzang undertook arduous journey to India to seek Buddhist texts, studying at Nalanda for 17 years. He brought back many scriptures and translated them into Chinese, writing 'Great Tang Records on the Western Regions,' providing valuable information about ancient India.

events.title: Arabs Invade Sindh
events.description: Arab general Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh region (modern Pakistan), marking Islam's first entry into Indian subcontinent.

events.title: Chola Dynasty (South India)
events.description: Chola Dynasty ruled South India and Sri Lanka, launching expeditions to Southeast Asia. Maritime trade flourished, spreading Indian culture to Southeast Asia. Built magnificent structures like Thanjavur Grand Temple.

events.title: Mahmud's Invasions of India
events.description: Mahmud of Ghazni repeatedly invaded northern India, plundering wealth and destroying Hindu temples. These invasions accelerated Islam's spread in India.

events.title: Delhi Sultanate Established
events.description: Qutb al-Din Aibak established Delhi Sultanate, beginning Muslim rule era in northern India. Delhi Sultanate experienced multiple dynasties, ruling India for about 320 years.

events.title: Vijayanagara Empire (South India)
events.description: Vijayanagara Empire was the last major Hindu empire in South India, resisting the southward expansion of Islamic Delhi Sultanate. Culture flourished, reaching its peak in the 16th century.

events.title: Vijayanagara Empire Founded
events.description: Vijayanagara Empire in southern India was established, becoming important Hindu kingdom resisting northern Muslim expansion. Empire reached zenith in 16th century with magnificent capital.

events.title: Vasco da Gama Arrives in India
events.description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama sailed around Cape of Good Hope from Europe to reach Calicut, India, opening sea route from Europe to India. This marked beginning of European colonial powers entering India.

events.title: Mughal Empire Established
events.description: Babur defeated the Delhi Sultanate at the Battle of Panipat and established the Mughal Empire. The Mughal Empire became India's most powerful Islamic dynasty, ruling the Indian subcontinent for over 300 years.

events.title: Reign of Akbar the Great
events.description: During Akbar's reign, he implemented religious tolerance policies, promoting harmony between Hindus and Muslims. He reformed administrative and tax systems, expanded territory, bringing the Mughal Empire to its zenith.

events.title: British East India Company Founded
events.description: Britain established East India Company, beginning trade activities in India. Initially just commercial organization, it gradually acquired political and military power, becoming Britain's tool for colonizing India.

events.title: Shah Jahan's Reign
events.description: During Shah Jahan's reign, Mughal architecture reached its peak. He built the world-famous Taj Mahal for his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. This white marble mausoleum became India's most famous building and a World Heritage Site.

events.title: Aurangzeb's Reign
events.description: Aurangzeb was last great Mughal emperor. He was devout Muslim, abandoned religious tolerance policy, imposed Islamic law and Jizya tax, triggering Hindu resentment. After his death, Mughal Empire rapidly declined.

events.title: Maratha Empire
events.description: Shivaji established Maratha Empire, resisting Mughal rule. Marathas became 18th century India's most powerful force, once controlling most of India, until defeated by British East India Company.

events.title: Persian Invasion of Delhi
events.description: Persian ruler Nadir Shah invaded Delhi, plundering the city and taking massive treasures including the famous Peacock Throne and Koh-i-Noor diamond. This accelerated Mughal Empire's decline.

events.title: Mughal Empire Declines
events.description: After Aurangzeb's death, Mughal Empire fell into decline. Multiple regions declared independence, Persian Nadir Shah and Afghan Ahmad Shah invaded, plundering Delhi. Empire existed in name only.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.description: The British East India Company defeated the Nawab of Bengal at the Battle of Plassey, marking the beginning of British colonial rule in India. This was a crucial turning point in Britain's conquest of India.

events.title: Sepoy Mutiny (First War of Independence)
events.description: Indian soldiers in East India Company army launched large-scale uprising, quickly spreading across northern India. Though eventually suppressed, this was India's first major armed resistance against British colonialism.

events.title: Direct British Rule Begins
events.description: After the failure of the Indian Rebellion (also called the Sepoy Mutiny), the British government dissolved the East India Company and established direct rule over India. India became 'British India,' with Queen Victoria becoming Empress of India.

events.title: Indian National Congress Founded
events.description: Indian National Congress was founded in Bombay, becoming main political organization of India's independence movement. Congress initially only demanded more self-governance rights, later evolving into completely independent political party.

events.title: Partition of Bengal
events.description: British divided Bengal into West Bengal (Hindu majority) and East Bengal (Muslim majority), triggering widespread protests. This was first time British openly used 'divide and rule' strategy, but revoked in 1911 due to fierce opposition.

events.title: Gandhi Returns to India
events.description: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa and began leading the Indian independence movement. He advocated non-violent non-cooperation, becoming the spiritual leader of India's independence movement.

events.title: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
events.description: British troops opened fire on peaceful protesters in Amritsar's Jallianwala Bagh, killing about 400-1000 people. This massacre shocked India and world, greatly stimulating India's independence movement.

events.title: Non-Cooperation Movement
events.description: Gandhi launched first non-cooperation movement, calling on Indians to boycott British goods, courts, and schools. This was first mass civil disobedience movement in Indian independence struggle.

events.title: Salt March
events.description: Gandhi led the 'Salt March,' walking approximately 400 km from Ahmedabad to the sea to make salt, protesting Britain's salt monopoly. This non-violent protest drew international attention, becoming an iconic event of India's independence movement.

events.title: Pakistan Resolution
events.description: Muslim League passed Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution), formally proposing creation of independent Muslim state. This laid groundwork for later India-Pakistan partition.

events.title: Quit India Movement
events.description: Gandhi launched 'Quit India' movement, demanding British immediate withdrawal from India. This was final phase of Indian independence movement. British arrested large numbers of Congress leaders, but movement continued.

events.title: Bengal Famine
events.description: Severe famine occurred in Bengal region, causing approximately 3 million deaths. Main causes included war, natural disasters, and British colonial policy failures.

events.title: Indian Independence
events.description: India gained independence, with Jawaharlal Nehru becoming the first Prime Minister. However, the Indian subcontinent was simultaneously partitioned into India and Pakistan, triggering massive religious conflicts and population migrations, with hundreds of thousands dying.

events.title: First Indo-Pakistani War
events.description: India and Pakistan went to war over Kashmir issue. War ended with UN ceasefire, Kashmir divided into Indian-controlled and Pakistani-controlled regions. Kashmir issue remains unresolved dispute between two countries.

events.title: Assassination of Gandhi
events.description: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated in New Delhi by a Hindu extremist. Gandhi's death shocked the nation, and India lost its greatest spiritual leader.

events.title: Ambedkar Drafts Constitution
events.description: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Dalit leader and jurist, chaired Drafting Committee and drafted India's Constitution. He fought for equality and rights of low-caste people, making enormous contributions to Indian democracy and human rights.

events.title: Republic Constitution Takes Effect
events.description: India's Constitution officially came into effect, making India a sovereign democratic republic. This constitution is the world's longest written constitution, establishing parliamentary democracy, federalism, and secular state principles.

events.title: First Five-Year Plan
events.description: India implemented first Five-Year Plan, led by Prime Minister Nehru. India adopted mixed economy model, combining planned economy and market economy, focusing on industrialization and agricultural development.

events.title: Sino-Indian Border War
events.description: China and India fought war over border disputes in Himalayan region. India suffered defeat, losing territory. This war deeply impacted Sino-Indian relations for decades.

events.title: Second Indo-Pakistani War
events.description: India and Pakistan went to war again over Kashmir. War ended in stalemate under UN and USSR mediation, Kashmir issue remained unresolved.

events.title: Indira Gandhi Era
events.description: Indira Gandhi (Nehru's daughter) served as Prime Minister twice. She implemented 'Green Revolution', promoted India's nuclear program, but also imposed state of emergency, suppressing opposition. She was assassinated in 1984.

events.title: Third Indo-Pakistani War
events.description: India intervened in East Pakistan (Bangladesh) independence war, defeated Pakistan. East Pakistan became independent Bangladesh. This was decisive victory for India over Pakistan.

events.title: First Nuclear Test
events.description: India conducted first nuclear test 'Smiling Buddha', becoming sixth nuclear-weapon state. India called it 'peaceful nuclear explosion', but caused international concern.

events.title: State of Emergency
events.description: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi declared state of emergency, suspending civil liberties, imprisoning opposition, media censored. This was darkest period of Indian democracy. Emergency lifted in 1977, Gandhi lost election.

events.title: Operation Blue Star and Indira Gandhi Assassination
events.description: Indian army stormed Golden Temple in Amritsar to eliminate Sikh militants, causing many casualties. Indira Gandhi was subsequently assassinated by two Sikh bodyguards, triggering anti-Sikh riots killing thousands.

events.title: Economic Liberalization Reforms
events.description: India began implementing economic liberalization reforms amid severe economic crisis, deregulating, opening markets, and attracting foreign investment. This marked a major shift in India's economic policy.

events.title: Babri Masjid Destruction
events.description: Hindu nationalists destroyed Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, triggering nationwide Hindu-Muslim riots killing about 2,000. This incident heightened religious tensions in India.

events.title: Nuclear Tests
events.description: India conducted series of nuclear tests, officially declaring nuclear-weapon state status. Pakistan immediately responded with own nuclear tests, triggering South Asian nuclear arms race.

events.title: Kargil War
events.description: India and Pakistan fought limited war in Kargil region of Kashmir. India eventually regained control of occupied areas. This was first conflict between two nuclear powers.

events.title: IT Industry Boom
events.description: India's IT industry rapidly developed, Bangalore became 'Silicon Valley of India'. Indian IT companies and engineers made important contributions globally, India became major global IT outsourcing center.

events.title: Mumbai Terror Attacks
events.description: Pakistani terrorist organization Lashkar-e-Taiba launched large-scale terrorist attacks in Mumbai, attacking hotels, train stations, Jewish centers, killing about 170. This was India's worst terrorist attack.

events.title: Modi Becomes Prime Minister
events.description: The Bharatiya Janata Party won the general election, and Narendra Modi became Prime Minister. Modi promoted economic reform programs like 'Make in India' and adopted a more assertive foreign policy.

events.title: Demonetization
events.description: Modi government suddenly announced demonetization of 500 and 1000 rupee notes, aiming to combat corruption and black money. This caused economic chaos and controversy.

events.title: Kashmir Status Changed
events.description: Modi government revoked Article 370 of Constitution, abolishing Jammu and Kashmir's special autonomous status, changing it to Union Territory. This triggered controversy domestically and internationally.

events.title: COVID-19 Response
events.description: India implemented nationwide lockdown to combat COVID-19. Second wave in 2021 was severe, making India one of worst-affected countries globally. However, India also became major vaccine producer.

events.title: Hindu Nationalism Rise
events.description: Under Modi government, Hindu nationalism significantly rose. BJP promoted 'Hindutva' ideology, minority rights (especially Muslims) faced challenges. India's secular democracy under pressure.

events.title: Population Surpasses China
events.description: UN data showed India's population surpassed China's, making India the world's most populous country with approximately 1.42 billion people. This marked a significant shift in global population distribution.

events.title: Successful Lunar Mission
events.description: India's Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed in the lunar south polar region. India became the fourth nation to achieve a soft lunar landing and the first to land at the lunar south pole, demonstrating India's space technology advancement.
